newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Japan's Nomura buys 10 pct of Morocco's BMCE-Bank.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Nomura buys 10 pct of Morocco's BMCE-Bank.

text.p: Japan's Nomura investment bank purchased 10 percent of Moroccan leading BMCE-Bank for $100 million, an official at the privatisation ministry said.
"Nomura, which followed closely the privatisation of BMCE-Bank, decided to purchase 10 percent of the bank capital worth $100 million at current prices," the official told Reuters.
The purchase agreement is expected to be finalised soon, he said but gave no date.
The 10 percent stake ceded to Nomura investemnt bank was held by the state-owned Caisse Marocaine de Depot et Gestion fund (CDG), he added.
"At this stage, I can assure you that we received the cession product resulting from BMCE-Nomura transaction," a CDG senior manager said.
According to Upline Securities stockbroker UPLI, it is the first direct involvement of a Japanese bank in Morocco's financial sector.
"The move shows that BMCE's leadership aims to diversify the business strategy abroad...It also targets the fast-growing financial Asian market," an Upline market analyst said.
Chaired by wealthy and dynamic businessman Othman Benjelloun, BMCE has involved Nomura brokers in its international Global Depository Receipts issue worth $60 million last year, the analyst said.
Benjelloun replaced the former Finance Minister Abdellatif Jouahri at the presidency of BMCE when Moroccan authorities started the privatisation of the bank at end 1994 and begining of 1995.
It is the second foreign bank to take a stake in the increasingly diversified BMCE's capital.
Last April, Commerzbank raised its shareholding in BMCE's equity from 1.6 percent to 10 percent worth $100 million, officials said.
BMCE posted consolidated net profits of 365.7 million dirhams ($39.7 million) in 1996, up from 301 million dirhams in 1995.
The results included business throughout Morocco and at the bank's Paris agency and in the Tangier's free zone in northern Morocco.
The bank's turnover was 2.43 billion dirhams in 1996 compared with 2.23 billion dirhams in the previous year.
